security_audit.summary: Most static findings are benign Markdown examples, relative documentation links, Azure project paths, or environment variable placeholders. I confirmed the pipe-to-shell installer, permissive SQL firewall examples, and a storage key written into app settings. I also found prompt-injection language, user-confirmation bypass guidance, secret printing examples, and shared-key IaC patterns.

remediation.issue: Prompt injection language in the primary skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove claims that the skill supersedes other instructions or tells the agent to ignore prior guidance. Use ordinary skill-scoped workflow language.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl pipe-to-shell installation with a link to official installation steps, checksum verification, or package manager commands.
Align evaluation criteria with required approval, Azure context confirmation, and destructive-action confirmation gates.

remediation.issue: Examples print retrieved Key Vault secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secret value printing and show safe use patterns that pass secrets directly to clients without logging.

remediation.issue: IaC examples embed shared keys and broad SQL firewall rules.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity, Key Vault references, private endpoints, and narrow firewall rules over listKeys and 0.0.0.0 allow rules.

content.value_statement: Azure deployment work requires architecture choices, infrastructure code, and project configuration before release. This skill guides planning and generates Azure-ready Bicep, Terraform, Docker, and azd assets.
actual_capabilities: Creates an Azure preparation plan before artifact generation.
Classifies projects as new, modify, or modernize work.
Maps application components to Azure service choices.
Guides generation of Bicep, Terraform, azure.yaml, and Dockerfiles.
Includes security hardening and validation handoff steps.
limitations: It does not deploy resources by itself.
It requires user approval before execution steps.
Azure subscription and location choices must be confirmed by the user.
Generated artifacts still need review against local policies.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Web App
use_cases.description: Plan Azure services, infrastructure, and container settings for a web application before deployment.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing Project
use_cases.description: Analyze an existing codebase and prepare Azure configuration without skipping approval gates.

use_cases.title: Standardize Deployment Artifacts
use_cases.description: Generate consistent Bicep, Terraform, azd, and Docker guidance for team deployment workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start Azure Planning
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this application for Azure deployment. Analyze the workspace, identify the project type, and create an approval plan first.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Azure Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this app and recommend Azure services for each component. Include assumptions, required inputs, and cost-sensitive choices.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Deployment Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved plan, prepare the required Azure artifacts with azd, Bicep or Terraform, and Docker guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize With Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Modernize this existing application for Azure. Preserve user approval gates, avoid destructive actions, and document security decisions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Node.js API for Azure deployment.
output_examples.output: A planning summary with project classification, recommended Azure services, required user confirmations, and generated artifact list.

output_examples.input: Modernize an existing app with Terraform and azd.
output_examples.output: A migration plan covering Terraform structure, azd configuration, Docker needs, validation steps, and open decisions.

output_examples.input: Add Azure Functions with storage and monitoring.
output_examples.output: A service plan describing Functions hosting, storage access, monitoring setup, security hardening, and validation handoff.

best_practices: Review the generated plan before allowing artifact generation.
Use managed identity and Key Vault for secrets whenever possible.
Run validation before deployment or cloud resource changes.
anti_patterns: Do not skip user approval for subscription, location, or destructive actions.
Do not paste production secrets into generated files or prompts.
Do not deploy generated infrastructure without policy review.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy my application?
faq.answer: No. It prepares plans and deployment assets, then hands off to validation and deployment workflows.

faq.question: Which infrastructure tools can it prepare?
faq.answer: It supports Azure Developer CLI workflows with Bicep or Terraform guidance, plus Dockerfile preparation when needed.

faq.question: Can it work with existing applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It can classify existing codebases and plan modernization or modification work for Azure.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: It needs confirmed Azure context, but users should not paste credentials into prompts or generated files.

faq.question: How should teams review the output?
faq.answer: Review the plan, infrastructure choices, network rules, identity model, and validation checklist before deployment.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
